newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures surge higher by close in bounce back.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures surge higher by close in bounce back.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended sharply higher on a bounceback from what many see as an oversold condition despite diminishing fears of frost in Florida, traders said.
The market has recovered five cents in just two days, giving a healthy glow to charts, and Jim Cordier of Allendale added that speculative selling has ebbed.
Weather Services Corp said rains in the Florida citrus belt will probably continue through Wednesday, but no damaging cold weather was expected this week.
March orange juice settled 2.80 cents firmer at 82.35 cents per pound, traded 83.00 to 79.80 cents.
Volume was estimated at 3,500 lots compared to Monday's 2,765 lots.

"I think there is nobody left to sell this market," Cordier said. The seasonal low may well be over if there is follow through buying Wednesday, clearing the way for a push on the upside on the back of shortcovering.
"I would said we get into the 90s per pound basis March later this month," Cordier added.
Bernard Savaiko of PaineWebber said because of the oversold condition of the market, coupled with indications of a reversal, the covering of existing short positions appears warranted.
